asset: The Prep, Meshy text-to-motion test clip dance_prep_meshy for Nia and Marcus (#293)
status: test only. Not used by the game. Not reviewed by skaters or dancers.
credits: Motion generated by Meshy text-to-motion from an original text prompt by the project. No third-party motion or art is in it.

steps.prompt: Roller-rink stutter step moving slowly forward. Right foot steps short forward, knees bent; left foot crosses behind the right and the left toe taps behind the right heel. Hands clap in front of the chest as the hips dip and the head nods. Left foot uncrosses and steps forward; repeat. Left foot always crosses behind. Torso upright, small twist to the clap. Feet low. 100 BPM.
steps.result: clip.fbx, SMPL-H skeleton (52 joints), 120 frames at 30 fps, with a default Meshy mannequin mesh
assets/dances/meshy-293/prep/source-smplh.glb: the Meshy skeleton and motion with no mesh (the FBX is 16.8 MB and is not in git)

actions: Imported the shipped assets/skaters/<name>/skater.glb (Mixamo rig) and source-smplh.glb.
Picked the source window that loops best between 24 and 64 frames: start frame 6, 58 frames (62.1 BPM for 2 beats), seam cost 0.4981 m.

Copied the world rotation change of each SMPL-H joint onto the matching Mixamo bone. The toe bone stays at rest (rigid skate boot). Scaled the hip motion by the leg length and removed the drift of the hips.
Closed the loop seam and retimed the window to 48 frames at 30 fps (2 clip beats of 0.8 s, the same as the hand-keyed dances).
Leg IK from scripts/blender/nia_clips.py: the ankles stay at the rest height and the feet stay flat (only the yaw of the motion), so the wheels stay on the ground. Baked to plain bone keys.
Exported only the skeleton and the clip.
